korTTY manages SSH, Mosh and KTPH000local-shellKTPH001 connections through three entry points: KTPH002Quick ConnectKTPH003, the KTPH004Connection ManagerKTPH005, and saved KTPH006ProjectsKTPH007.

Open with KTPH003KTPH001KTPH004+KTPH005KTPH002KTPH006 (or KTPH007Connections → Quick Connect…KTPH008). Enter host, port, username and authentication, and connect without saving. Frequently used connections appear as quick buttons; a live search filters them. Saved connections can be picked from a dropdown with its own search field that matches name, host or KTPH009tagKTPH010 (KTPH000 works as a wildcard); a saved connection's tag is shown next to its name (🏷) in the dropdown and in the quick buttons' tooltips.

KTPH001Connections → Manage Connections…KTPH002 opens a searchable tree of saved connections (optionally grouped); the search field matches name, host, IP address or KTPH003tagKTPH004, with KTPH000 as a wildcard. From here you create, edit, duplicate, delete, tag, import and export connections.
The connection editor has these tabs:

Host, port, username, protocol (SSH / Mosh / Local Shell), authentication (password / key / keyboard-interactive), KTPH000Host key verificationKTPH001 (use default / verify / don't verify), group/folder assignment and an optional free-text KTPH002tagKTPH003. For KTPH004Local ShellKTPH005 connections host, port, username and authentication are not required and are disabled.
Per-connection colors, font, ANSI/TrueColor handling, terminal effect
Writes this connection's terminal output to a file — folder, format, daily rotation, compression and retention. See KTPH000Terminal loggingKTPH001.
Per-connection KTPH000session journalKTPH001: enable journaling for this connection and configure its capture log and AI summarization
Per-connection AI defaults: the KTPH000AI profileKTPH001 and AI Skills used by terminal AI features on this connection

Every saved connection can carry one optional free-text KTPH003tagKTPH004 — a label such as KTPH000, KTPH001 or a customer name — independent of the group/folder hierarchy. Set it on the connection editor's KTPH005ConnectionKTPH006 tab (next to the group), or in bulk in the Connection Manager. Tags are stored with the connection in KTPH002 and survive duplicating, exporting and importing.

KTPH000VisibleKTPH001 — tagged connections show a 🏷 badge after their name in the Connection Manager tree and in Quick Connect's saved-connections dropdown; the tag also appears in the tooltip of the frequently-used quick buttons.
KTPH000SearchableKTPH001 — the Connection Manager search (local and Teamwork tabs) and Quick Connect's saved-connections search match tags as well as names and hosts.

KTPH000Bulk assign / removeKTPH001 — select one or more servers and choose KTPH002Assign TagKTPH003 from the context menu to tag them in one step. The prompt is pre-filled when all selected connections already share the same tag, and clearing that pre-filled value removes the tag. KTPH004Remove TagKTPH005 clears the tag and is enabled only while the selection contains at least one tagged connection. The same two entries on a folder's context menu apply to every connection in that folder, subfolders included.

KTPH000Export by tagKTPH001 — once at least one tag exists, the Connection Manager's export dialog offers a KTPH002Connections to exportKTPH003 choice: keep the pre-selected connections, or export KTPH004all connections with these tagsKTPH005 — pick one or more tags from the list, the header's connection count follows the selection live, and the export button stays disabled while nothing matches.
Standard SSH via Apache MINA SSHD. Supports password, public-key and keyboard-interactive authentication, keep-alive, and OSC 8 clickable hyperlinks.
Roaming, latency-friendly Mosh transport (mosh4j). The Mosh backend is bundled in native builds; existing connections need no migration.

Opens the KTPH000local machine'sKTPH001 shell in a terminal tab (no network) via a pty4j-backed pseudo-terminal. Host, port, username and authentication are not required. See KTPH002Local ShellKTPH003 below.

Interactive Terminal and SFTP connections use the same trust-on-first-use (TOFU) host-key store. Mosh uses it for the SSH bootstrap as well. Trust is keyed by the normalized host name and port, so different saved connections to the same endpoint share one decision.

On the first connection, korTTY shows the key algorithm and OpenSSH SHA-256 fingerprint. Verify that fingerprint with the server administrator before selecting KTPH000YesKTPH001; KTPH002NoKTPH003 is the safe default. A matching key is accepted silently on later connections. If the server presents a different key, korTTY hard-blocks the connection, shows the expected and offered fingerprints, and does not retry because repeating the attempt cannot resolve a possible man-in-the-middle attack.

The first-use prompt can be turned off for hosts where it is not wanted — set KTPH000Host key verificationKTPH001 on the connection editor's KTPH002ConnectionKTPH003 tab or in Quick Connect (KTPH004Use defaultKTPH005 / KTPH006VerifyKTPH007 / KTPH008Don't verifyKTPH009), per group via the Connection Manager's group context menu, or globally under KTPH010Settings → TerminalKTPH011. The relaxation is accept-new only: an unknown key is pinned without a prompt, but a key that differs from one already pinned for that host is still hard-blocked. See KTPH012Relaxing host-key verificationKTPH013.

The interactive pins are stored atomically in KTPH000, with cross-process locking so two korTTY windows cannot overwrite each other's decisions. These endpoint-based pins are separate from the connection-ID-based pins used by unattended JobScheduler SSH, SFTP, and Rsync jobs.

When a new split connection is opened, the SSH handshake runs on a worker while a progress dialog keeps the JavaFX interface responsive. This allows both host-key confirmation and keyboard-interactive authentication to complete without blocking the UI.

A KTPH000Local ShellKTPH001 connection spawns a local pseudo-terminal (PTY) on your own machine instead of connecting to a remote host. It is selectable in both KTPH002Quick ConnectKTPH003 and the KTPH004Connection ManagerKTPH005; for these connections host, port, username and authentication are not required (and are disabled in the dialogs), and no password prompt is shown.

KTPH002PowerShellKTPH003 (default) or KTPH004cmd.exeKTPH005. KTPH006Git BashKTPH007, KTPH008CygwinKTPH009 and KTPH010WSLKTPH011 are also offered as presets — but only when actually installed (Git Bash/Cygwin are detected via their usual install locations / KTPH000; WSL appears only when KTPH001 is present and at least one distribution is installed).
Defaults to your KTPH000 (falling back to KTPH001 or KTPH002).

A free-form KTPH003Custom commandKTPH004 field accepts any executable with arguments (e.g. KTPH000, KTPH001, a Git Bash path), and an optional KTPH005start directoryKTPH006 can be set. The command parser is quote-aware, so shell paths containing spaces — like KTPH002 — launch correctly.

Terminal logging and recording, plus the AI input/data hooks, work for local shells via a shared KTPH000 interface. Typed and pasted agent requests use the same byte-level input path, and terminal file actions plus local agent runs follow the interactive shell's current directory. macOS/Linux use the local process directory; native PowerShell and cmd use absolute prompt paths. WSL, Git Bash, Cygwin, and custom commands are best-effort when their shell path namespace differs from the host filesystem, and an unmappable directory produces an explicit error instead of a wrong-file fallback. Features that depend on an SSH channel stay SSH-only.
The KTPH000AI AgentKTPH001 and KTPH002AI PlanningKTPH003 also run in local shells on Windows, macOS and Linux — see KTPH004AI assistantKTPH005.
KTPH003SSH tunnelsKTPH004 — forward ports through the connection: KTPH005localKTPH006 (KTPH000), KTPH007remoteKTPH008 (KTPH001) or KTPH009dynamic / SOCKSKTPH010 (KTPH002).
KTPH000Jump server (bastion)KTPH001 — route the connection through an intermediate host; SSH terminal and SFTP sessions both hop through it. See KTPH002Jump ServerKTPH003.

KTPH000Connections → Import…KTPH001 reads connection files from KTPH002MTPuTTYKTPH003, KTPH004MobaXtermKTPH005 and KTPH006PuTTY Connection ManagerKTPH007, with group filtering and credential handling.

This page is part of the scaffolded guide. The full feature library — SFTP, snippets, JobScheduler, AI assistant KTPH000 tools, terminal recording, security, and the complete settings tables — is being filled in next.
